maria: Heads up — canary deploy of 4-bit kernels on dedicated-pool-2 is showing a sustained throughput drop (~20%) and memory churn on a subset of NF4 models. Not a spike, steady regression since 03:10 UTC.
kevin: omg, saw alerts. Is this the kernel_dispatch_v2 rollout?
anika: yes, we flipped kernel_dispatch_v2 + mixed-precision routing for canary traffic at 03:05. Only applied to nf4/fp4 paths.
perfbot: perf-alert: canary=dedicated-pool-2, model-family=llama-variant, metric=throughput, delta=-22%, window=10m, p95_latency=+46%
sam: dump logs? any OOMs or large GC events?
maria: no OOMs, but KV cache eviction rate is much higher. Seeing small, frequent evictions + allocation churn. Putting a short snippet: ```[2026-03-18T03:12:07Z] kernel_dispatch_v2: selected kernel=4bit_prefetch_fast, fallback=fp16_mul_add, kv_evicts=328, kv_hits=4021, gpu_mem_used=38.7GB -> 41.2GB```
jordan: kv_evicts that high for small batch sizes smells like fragmentation/allocator mismatch after switching kernel code paths. Did we change slab sizing for 4-bit gemms?
anika: we changed the quantized-kv alignment to 128 bytes (was 64) to satisfy new vectorized kernels. That could double small allocations.
infra-bot: deploy-log: rolled kernel_dispatch_v2 to canary (deploy id d-2026-03-18-0310). previous deploy d-2026-03-18-0300 rolled back.
kevin: if alignment bumped, small KV entries might now occupy 2x space — that explains mem bump and more evictions -> throughput drop due to cache misses. Can we repro locally with our microbench?
sam: starting a microbench with seq-len distribution and mixed batch sizes to simulate realistic traffic. will run kernels: 4bit_prefetch_fast, 4bit_slowpath, fp16_fallback.
maria: profiling traces attached in S3 (link) — key observation: kernel selection oscillates per-request when prefix length changes, causing repeated kernel swaps and frequent KV slab fragmentation.
anj: (typo) anika: also saw higher kernel launch overhead when tiny batches hit new kernels; launch+sync cost dominates for <8 tokens.
perfbot: profiling-summary: avg_kernel_switches_per_request=2.3, avg_kernel_launch_ms=1.8, kv_eviction_rate=0.9/s, throughput_down=21%
jordan: suggestion: revert kernel_dispatch_v2's aggressive alignment change, or add a fast-path that preserves old slab layout for small KV entries.
anika: we can gate alignment change behind `small_kv_preserve=true` flag. Quick patch might restore density.
kevin: agree — also add hysteresis to kernel selection so we don't flip kernels based on 1-2 token prefix deltas. That should cut switches.
sam: microbench results: with alignment reverted throughput returns to baseline, p95 latency back to normal. With hysteresis only, throughput improves ~12% (not full), but evictions drop 60%.
maria: good — plan: (1) rollback alignment in canary, (2) add selection hysteresis + birds-eye telemetry, (3) run extended canary 2h, (4) if stable, promote. Any objections?
anika: sounds good. I'll open a PR for alignment rollback + flag, and a follow-up for hysteresis.
kevin: I'll prep rollout playbook and metrics to watch (kv_eviction_rate, kernel_switches, throughput, p95).
perfbot: action-created: ticket INF-4729 (rollback alignment + hysteresis).
infra-bot: canary rollback initiated (d-2026-03-18-0332), will monitor for 30m.
maria: thanks all — documenting root cause as "allocation alignment increase + aggressive kernel switching -> KV fragmentation -> increased evictions -> throughput regression". We'll keep timeline in the ticket. :thumbsup:
